observed_original_abi.calling_convention: __thiscall, with callee stack cleanup: THREE 4-byte stack words, 12 bytes in all, popped by the callee. The machine-derived ABI record (evidence pack reconstruction/evidence/0052e640/evidence.json, category abi_derived) DETERMINES the convention rather than abstaining: conventions.calling_convention = __thiscall, conventions.confidence = INFERRED, conventions.candidate_conventions = [__thiscall], conventions.ambiguities = []. It does so in two steps it records separately. R1-VFT (INFERRED) puts the receiver in ECX: 0x0052e640 is slot 8 of the sound vptr-backed vftable at 0x013f2194, one of 25 such tables, so it is a virtual member of some class, and the body reads the incoming ECX before writing it; the rule also records why that read decides the matter, because the callee pops its own stack arguments - the COM/__stdcall interface form - which is the one shape in which a virtual member takes its receiver from the first popped stack word instead and never reads its incoming ECX. C6B (INFERRED) then names __thiscall from the callee-side cleanup, which rules out cdecl and fastcall, together with the receiver register. The confidence is INFERRED and is reported as such, not upgraded to OBSERVED. The reconstructed entry is a naked __thiscall member, so the source span carries a __thiscall token, and its own `ret $12` performs the callee-side cleanup the machine performs.
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The determination is INFERRED, not OBSERVED, and the two are kept apart throughout. What the machine observes is the stack discipline: cleanup.bytes = 12, cleanup.side = "callee", cleanup.evidence = "ret 0xc", at OBSERVED confidence, corroborated independently from the caller side because both direct call sites (0x0050a468 and 0x0050a5d6) push exactly three dwords and issue no ADD ESP after the CALL. What the machine infers is the convention and the receiver register, and it does so from the vftable membership plus the callee-side cleanup, at INFERRED confidence with no ambiguities left open. The __thiscall claim is corroborated from the caller side as well, independently of the vftable rule: both call sites load ECX from the caller's own captured receiver (its entry capture MOV [EBP-0x2c],ECX at 0x0050a0a9) immediately before the call, which is what __thiscall requires. The sibling predicate 0x0050a920, called from the same block, has the same shape with four popped words and does dereference its ECX, so the ECX-capture prologue is a receiver idiom in this neighbourhood. __stdcall is now excluded as well: it is the form that would take the receiver from the first popped stack word, and this body reads its incoming ECX instead, which is exactly the discriminator rule R1-VFT records. Ghidra cross-validation remains no_information (ghidra_calling_convention null, parameter_count 0) and is not relied on.
observed_original_abi.return_width_observation: XOR AL,AL at 0x0052e647 writes the low byte of EAX only, so bits 8..31 of EAX are undefined on exit. observed_original_abi.stack_arguments_observation: Three dwords of entry_ESP+0x4 / +0x8 / +0xc are popped by the callee. Both call sites push exactly three dwords, which corroborates the count from the caller side. observed_original_abi.receiver_observation: ECX is read at 0x0052e643 (PUSH ECX) and written to the frame slot [EBP-0x4] at 0x0052e644. The slot is never reloaded, so the capture is dead: no instruction in the body can make the incoming ECX influence the answer. The machine's receiver record now names ECX as the receiver register at INFERRED confidence with provenance vftable_slot_dispatch, so ECX IS the receiver; what remains open is what the receiver IS, and nothing about that is claimed. observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX carries the receiver, at INFERRED confidence, with the machine's own label for how it determined that: receiver.provenance = vftable_slot_dispatch. The record states receiver.present = true, receiver.register = ECX, receiver.bounds_only = true, receiver.shape = null, receiver.distinct_offsets = 0, receiver.written_through = 0. What the body itself shows is only the WIDTH of the receiver: one 4-byte word, the width of PUSH ECX at 0x0052e643. It is read (PUSH ECX, and then MOV dword ptr [EBP + -0x4],ECX at 0x0052e644) and never dereferenced, so the capture is dead in this body and no instruction in it can make the incoming ECX influence the answer. Because the body never dereferences the word, no field offset is claimed in either direction: the only memory operand in the whole listing is the callee's own frame slot at [EBP + -0x4], based on EBP, and that is a frame slot and not a field of anything. The earlier record said of this that "the engine declines to call ECX a receiver" and "this reconstruction does not call it one either"; that is no longer true and is withdrawn. What is still NOT claimed, and is not claimed by the convention either, is the receiver's identity: no owning class, no receiver type, no object shape, no object size, no vtable-pointer offset, no SDK method name. R1-VFT names ONE table and slot (0x013f2194, slot 8) as the evidence for the receiver and counts 25 tables holding this address; a slot index is not a class, the binary has no MSVC RTTI, and the other 24 tables are not individually attributed here. The reconstructed entry therefore carries the receiver as the plain 4-byte word the machine proves and names nothing beyond that width.

data_pointer_evidence.summary: The address of this function is stored as a dword in .rdata at five measured sites, four of them verified by live memory read in this session. That is machine evidence of participation in a data table; it is NOT evidence of a class, a slot offset, or a virtual dispatch, none of which is claimed.
data_pointer_evidence.not_asserted: no owning class, no table base, and no SDK method name. Two adjacent equal slots in one repeating record and single slots in two other tables is the shape a shared folded default body has, and it is equally the shape a per-class default has; the record does not separate the two. The derived record's own 25-table membership count and its naming of 0x013f2194 slot 8 are the RULE's bookkeeping - the evidence it used to place the receiver in ECX - and are not adopted here as an attribution of a slot offset or a class. No field offset is claimed in either direction for the same reason: the body never dereferences the receiver, and the only memory operand in the listing is the callee's own frame slot at [EBP + -0x4].

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The 15-byte body is reconstructed in full and the entry is a naked __thiscall member, so the source span carries the __thiscall token the machine-derived ABI record names at INFERRED confidence. Claimed: the calling convention (__thiscall, INFERRED), the receiver register (ECX, INFERRED, provenance vftable_slot_dispatch), the callee-side cleanup of three 4-byte words (12 bytes, OBSERVED), the one-byte zero return, the single frame-local store, and the straight-line control flow - all of which the 8-instruction listing and the derived record support. NOT claimed: any semantic name, any owning class, any receiver type, any field name, any field offset, and any vtable slot offset beyond the single slot the derivation itself names as its evidence (0x013f2194 slot 8). The convention says where the receiver arrives, not what it is.
preserved_semantics: the answer is the byte 0 and only the byte 0; bits 8..31 of EAX are left as the caller left them, which is why the declared return type is one byte and why the model test compares the high 24 bits against the sentinel it pushed

the callee pops 12 bytes of stack arguments, so the entry declares a receiver plus three dword parameters and its own `ret $12` performs the pop; the model test drives it through a bare-assembly __thiscall call site and requires the stack pointer to land back exactly where it started

ECX is read and captured to a frame slot, and never dereferenced, so any receiver word including null and including an unreadable one is accepted; the model test passes the word 1 and the word at the top of the address space
the three popped argument words are read by nothing, so the answer is 0 for every argument triple; the model test sweeps a spread of all three
no callee, no global, no branch, no memory operand outside its own frame
body_reconstruction.byte_exactness: Not claimed for the model: the reconstruction is not an MSVC build. The entry is spelled as a naked __thiscall body and the emitted sequence is instruction for instruction the original 15 bytes, but three encodings differ because each pair of spellings denotes the same operation: the original encodes the two frame-pointer moves as 8b ec / 8b e5 (mov r32,r/m32) where GAS picks 89 e5 / 89 ec (mov r/m32,r32), and it encodes the zeroing as 32 c0 (XOR r8,r/m8) where GAS picks 30 c0. A default position-independent build additionally prepends a ten-byte __x86.get_pc_thunk.ax PC anchor (g++ -m32 -fPIC; clang++ -m32 emits none), which is a toolchain artifact and not part of the reconstruction. The model test pins this rather than papering over it: the nine bytes with a single spelling must match 0x0052e640's bytes exactly, each divergent pair must be one of the two encodings of the same operation, and an anchor is recognised by its exact opcode pair and the target bytes are then required immediately after it. A toolchain emitting some other form of anchor fails rather than passes. A second, independent witness carries the literal original encodings as .byte directives and is compared against the same 15 bytes with no allowance at all.

semantic_findings: The whole observable contract is 'answer the byte 0'. There is no input that reaches the answer: ECX is captured and dropped, the three popped argument words are never read, and there is no branch, callee, global or memory access outside the frame.

Bits 8..31 of EAX are undefined on exit, because the body writes AL alone. Both observed consumers read AL alone, so the byte is the contract and the dword is not. The model test pins this by pushing a sentinel into EAX and requiring its high 24 bits to come back unchanged.
The JNZ at 0x0050a472 and the JNZ at 0x0050a5e0 that follow the two direct calls are statically dead. Both call sites are asking a predicate whose answer is always no.

The port is fixed from the caller side: both call sites push exactly three dwords, set ECX from the caller's own captured receiver and do not adjust ESP afterwards, which is three popped words, a register-carried receiver and callee cleanup. The machine-derived record now reaches the same conclusion independently and at INFERRED confidence, naming __thiscall (rule C6B) on the strength of the receiver rule R1-VFT, and it excludes __stdcall on the recorded ground that a body in that form takes its receiver from the first popped stack word and never reads its incoming ECX - which is what this body does. The two routes agree, which is the point: neither rests on the other.

The immediate neighbours 0x0052e620 (RET 0xc) and 0x0052e650 (RET 0x4) share the prologue PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / PUSH ECX / MOV [EBP-0x4],ECX and have no body at all, and 0x0052e680 shares it and uses the captured ECX as a receiver throughout. The prologue is the local idiom of a family of member-shaped functions, and 0x0052e640 is one of its empty-bodied members that still answers. That the same idiom appears on a body that uses the receiver and on one that does not is what keeps the receiver's IDENTITY open here while its REGISTER is not: the prologue is shared, the use is not.

Its address is stored as a dword at six measured .rdata sites, twice as a pair of adjacent equal slots inside a repeating 20-byte record, and the derived record independently places it in 25 sound vptr-backed vftables. Combined with the empty body, that is the shape of a shared default body; a per-class default body would store it the same way, and the record does not separate the two.

The convention narrows what the answer is not asked about. __thiscall is a claim about how the function is REACHED, and it fixes the receiver's register and the stack discipline completely; it says nothing about what the receiver is, and nothing in the body or the record identifies it. The reconstruction therefore claims the port and declines the identity, and the two are kept in separate fields so that neither can be read as the other.
unresolved_questions: What predicate does this answer, and to which question? The body is a constant no; nothing in the evidence names the question. The two direct callers both discard the answer into a statically dead branch, so even the callers do not say. The __thiscall determination does not help: it fixes how the function is called, not what it is for.

Which class, if any, owns the vftable slots that point here? Six .rdata sites were read live and no table base and no slot offset was derived by this package. R1-VFT names 0x013f2194 slot 8 as the evidence FOR the receiver and counts 25 tables holding this address; that is the rule's own bookkeeping, not an attribution of an owning class, and the other 24 tables are not individually attributed. Ghidra's referenced_by_vtables list of 18 addresses is a classifier association, not a measured table base, and is not used as one.

Is the address a compiler-folded COMDAT shared by several unrelated 'return false' defaults, or one class's default emitted once? Both fit every observation, including the two adjacent equal slots and the 25-table membership count.

What IS the receiver? The convention fixes that ECX carries it and the record fixes that it is present, one 4-byte word wide, and never dereferenced here - so no field offset is claimed in either direction. But the receiver's type, object size, shape and owning class are all unproven, and the body cannot show them because it never looks. That is now the sharpest open question rather than the register, and it stays open.

Are the three popped dwords really three parameters? The derived record marks all three observed=false and the caller corroborates the count by pushing three, but the body reads none of them, so the count is the popped area rather than a read parameter count. The reconstruction keeps three because `ret 0xc` pops three, not because three parameters were proven.

Is the C return type bool, unsigned char or std::uint8_t? The machine fixes only the width (one byte of EAX, upper 24 bits undefined) and the value (0). The reconstruction uses std::uint8_t; the choice is source-side and is not verified.
Does the JNZ that follows each call site ever get a live value? Both are statically dead in this build, so no differential trace of the original process exists that could show the answer being used.

Why does a 218-instruction neighbour (0x0052e680) with the same prologue dereference its ECX while this one does not? Both shapes are observed here; which one the original author wrote for this slot is not recorded anywhere in the evidence. The determination that this one is a __thiscall member does not answer it, since the neighbour is a member too.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists in this repository for 0x0052e640, so every claim in this record is static. A differential run under Wine must confirm the answer is still 0 in the shipping build and that no runtime patch retargets the address.

One of the .rdata slots that point here must be observed being called with a concrete receiver before any owning class or slot offset can be named. The __thiscall determination does not satisfy this gate: it fixes the register the receiver arrives in, not the object behind it.

The INFERRED confidence of the convention and of the receiver register must not be reported as OBSERVED without a runtime observation of one of these vftable slots being called with a concrete receiver, which is the evidence the R1-VFT rule names as its own basis and the evidence a trace would supply directly.
